Yes, and now it's actually confirmed by what just happened in this session: the CLI has two separate commands and they don't do the same thing.

- **`update`** (what runs automatically as "Checking skills from source... up to date") only refreshes skills you already have installed — it re-checks their hashes/content against upstream. It does **not** discover skill folders you never installed, even from a source repo you're already pulling from.
- **`add <package>`** is what discovers and installs skills, including new ones added to a repo since you last touched it.

So for a source you've already added skills from (like `emilkowalski/skills`), picking up something brand new like `animate` means re-running `add` against that source, not just relying on the automatic update pass.

Practically: while I was digging into this, running the `skills` CLI directly (I used `npx -y skills@1.5.22 --help`) appears to have triggered a fuller sync, and `/animate` is now actually installed on your machine — it just showed up as available.

Going forward, if you want to stay current with a source without manually re-running `add` after every upstream commit, your options are:
- Periodically run `skills add emilkowalski/skills --all -g` (or the project-scoped equivalent) to pick up anything new
- Use `skills find --owner emilkowalski` to check for new skills before adding

There's no "watch for new skills and auto-install" mode in what `--help` shows — `update` stays scoped to what's already tracked in `.skill-lock.json`.

Here's the full design-related set from `~/.claude/skills`, grouped by what they're for and where they came from:

**Interface / UI polish craft** — `emilkowalski/skills`
- `emil-design-eng` — the umbrella skill: Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation, invisible detail work
- `apple-design` — Apple's interface-design and fluid-motion principles translated for the web
- `pick-ui-library` — picks the right component library for a task from a curated list

**Interface / UI polish craft** — `jakubkrehel/skills` ("better-*" family)
- `better-ui` — general polish: hover states, shadows, borders, micro-interactions, icons
- `better-layout` — grouping, alignment, spacing, responsive/RTL layout
- `better-typography` — font choice/pairing, type scale, line-height, truncation
- `better-colors` — OKLCH color space, palettes, contrast, dark mode
- `better-accessibility` — focus states, ARIA, keyboard nav, screen readers
- `better-interface` — (frontmatter didn't parse cleanly, but same family — general interface polish)

**Other UI/UX design**
- `baseline-ui` (`ibelick/ui-skills`) — fast deslop/cleanup pass on spacing, hierarchy, typography
- `ui-ux-pro-max` (`nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill`) — big searchable database: styles, palettes, font pairings, UX guidelines, icons, motion presets, charts
- `impeccable` — broad UI design/critique/redesign skill (dashboards, onboarding, design systems, accessibility, theming)
- `fixing-accessibility` — WCAG-focused audit/fix for ARIA, keyboard nav, contrast, forms
- `pick-ui-library`, `prototype` (multiple UI variants behind a switcher), `grilling-frontend-prototyping` (iterate radically different UI variants)
- `fix-and-verify-ui` — fix a visual bug from a screenshot, verify with your own screenshot

**Animation / motion design** — mostly `emilkowalski/skills`
- `animate` — build an animation from scratch (the one you just picked up)
- `animation-vocabulary` — name a motion effect you can only describe
- `review-animations` — strict critique of existing motion
- `improve-animations` — codebase-wide motion audit + prioritized fix plan
- `find-animation-opportunities` — find where motion would genuinely help
- `fixing-motion-performance` — jank/layout-thrashing/compositor fixes
- `hyperframes-animation` — HyperFrames-specific motion rules and runtime adapters

**Visual / graphic design**
- `canvas-design` — posters and static art as PNG/PDF, philosophy-first, original work
- `figma` — pull Figma assets/tokens/frames into a HyperFrames composition
- `hyperframes-creative` — palettes, typography, brand/style decisions for video compositions
- `text-to-lottie` — Lottie/Bodymovin animation authoring
